critical_code_review_comments: notifications.py: Fernet key is derived from JWT_SECRET via sha256. If JWT_SECRET ever rotates, all previously encrypted notification secrets become unrecoverable (dec() returns ''). Consider a dedicated NOTIF_ENC_KEY env var so secrets survive JWT rotation.

notifications.py send_smtp/discord/telegram lack explicit timeout fallback handling beyond client timeouts; httpx raise_for_status throws HTTPStatusError which is fine, but Discord/Telegram should validate webhook_url/bot_token format (basic URL check) before attempting send to give clearer 400 error rather than generic 500.

routers.py create_alert: when no camera_id is supplied it falls back to `db.cameras.find_one({})` (random first camera). For a real critical alert that's not tied to any camera, the alert ends up associated with an arbitrary camera. Consider leaving camera fields blank when none specified.

Notifications.jsx: save() sends the on-screen password value as-is even when the input shows the masked placeholder (placeholder is just placeholder, value stays empty when untouched, so this is OK — verified empty-preserve works). Good design.
Notifications.jsx line 15: `<input>` uses raw element instead of the shadcn Input — inconsistent with the rest of the app's styling system (minor).
BackgroundTasks dispatch on critical alert: failures inside send_notification are swallowed silently (no logging visible to user). Consider logging dispatch results to audit log for traceability.
